channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: RBA’s Bullock: Key question is whether tightening already delivered is enough to slow inflation
item.description: Speaking at the Anika Foundation Fundraising Lunch in Sydney on Tuesday, Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock said that the “key question is whether tightening already delivered is enough to slow inflation.”

item.title: Japan's Katayama: Need to communicate JGB market before budget compilation
item.description: In the Asian trading session on Tuesday, Japan Finance Minister (FM) Satsuki Katayama highlighted the need to communicate to financial and Japanese Government Bonds (JGBs) markets regarding the administration’s intentions towards the fiscal policy stance.

item.title: Asian stocks including KOSPI slide as AI doubts hit chipmakers
item.description: Asian stocks fall sharply on Tuesday as mounting skepticism over the massive financial returns on artificial intelligence spending triggered a widespread sell-off across global semiconductor shares.

item.title: Canadian Dollar struggles near two-week low vs USD amid bearish oil prices, ahead of FOMC
item.description: The USD/CAD pair enters a bullish consolidation phase near a two-week high, touched during the Asian session on Tuesday, and currently trades around 1.4120.

item.title: Australian Dollar gains ahead of RBA Governor Bullock’s speech
item.description: AUD/USD inches higher after recovering its daily losses, trading around 0.6990 during the Asian hours on Tuesday. Traders are keeping a close watch on scheduled remarks from Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock later in the day.

item.title: WTI consolidates near one-week low, around $81.00 as traders eye US–Iran talks
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – is seen consolidating the previous day's heavy losses and trading around the $81.00 mark, just above a one-week high set during the Asian session on Tuesday.

item.title: British Pound softens as Fed rate uncertainty supports US Dollar
item.description: GBP/USD edges lower after opening at a bullish gap, remaining within positive territory and trading around 1.3290 during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Euro hangs near monthly low, holds above 1.1350 as USD bulls pause ahead of FOMC meeting
item.description: The EUR/USD pair is seen consolidating near the monthly trough and trading just above mid-1.1300s during the Asian session on Tuesday. Traders seem hesitant and await the outcome of a two-day FOMC policy meeting before placing aggressive directional bets.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7928 vs. 6.7911 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Tuesday at 6.7928 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7911.

item.title: Gold declines despite easing concerns over inflation, interest rate hikes
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) loses ground after registering gains in the previous day, trading around $4,050 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Crude Oil buys its fourth peace of the year while the tankers stay parked
item.description: WTI Crude Oil trades just above $81.00 on Monday, down close to 9% from Friday's close near $89.00, having gapped more than $5.00 lower at the open and spent the session extending rather than repairing it.

item.title: Tokyo can still afford to defend the Japanese Yen, just not for very long
item.description: The Japanese Yen trades a little firmer on Monday, with USD/JPY down 0.05% and sitting short of 164.00 after last week's high stalled a hundredth of a Yen beneath the figure.

item.title: The Australian Dollar stops trading commodities and starts trading one number
item.description: The Australian Dollar trades just beneath 0.7000 on Monday, up around 0.1%, having covered less than 30 pips between its session high and its session low. For the better part of a fortnight the market has tried to make something of the 0.7000 area and given up each time.

item.title: Britain's best data week of the summer sends British Pound Sterling to a four-week low
item.description: British Pound Sterling trades beneath 1.3300 against the Dollar on Monday, roughly 0.3% lower on the day and back at ground it last held in the opening days of July. It gets there at the end of the strongest run of British data since the spring, which is the part worth sitting with.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: MAS tightening underpins Singapore Dollar – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that USD/SGD is consolidating around 1.2900 after pulling back from near 1.3000, as the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) unexpectedly tightened policy for a second consecutive meeting.

item.title: Trump urges Fed rate cuts as Gulf War ends, seen lowering prices
item.description: On Monday, late in the North American session, US President Donald Trump stated that there was a good inflation report recently, adding that costs were falling rapidly and that prices should drop significantly once the Gulf War ends.

item.title: US President Trump keeps Iran diplomacy alive after halting strikes
item.description: On Monday, US President Donald Trump grabbed the headlines as investors awaited monetary policy meetings by three of the eight major central banks, led by the Federal Reserve, the Bank of England, and the Bank of Japan.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Rangebound trade against US Dollar guided by PBoC fix – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong expect USD/CNH to stay broadly rangebound near term, with the daily People's Bank of China (PBoC) fix clustered around 6.79 and acting as an anchor rather than a directional signal.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar holds after weak US durable goods data
item.description: NZD/USD trades near the 0.5790 area on Monday, struggling to extend its recovery despite modest weakness in the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Hawkish MAS supports SGD against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan notes that the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) delivered a second consecutive tightening by slightly increasing the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) slope, reinforcing SGD resilience.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Political risks temper valuation case – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) and Jakarta equities underperformed after Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo unexpectedly resigned two years before his term ends, raising concerns about political interference.

item.title: Japanese Yen: BoJ tightening yet weaker JPY against US Dollar – BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas strategists see Japan’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth slowing to 0.8% in 2026 from 1.1% in 2025 as higher inflation and energy-related costs weigh on activity, partly offset by fiscal support and AI (Artificial intelligence) investment.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: MAS signals inflation concern – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay notes Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) unexpectedly tightened policy for a second meeting, slightly increasing the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER) slope and stressing the move was smaller than April’s.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar softens as Oil plunges on Middle East pause
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) traded mostly unchanged on Monday as a temporary pause in hostilities between the United States and Iran reduces demand for safe-haven assets. The US Dollar Index (DXY) traded lower earlier in the session but moved closed to breakeven by the late American afternoon.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Range holds as intervention fears bite
item.description: The EUR/JPY holds firm around 163.70 on Monday as the Japanese Yen strengthens, with investors cautious about opening fresh hawkish bets amid fears of intervention in the foreign exchange market.

item.title: LatAm FX: Carry appeal faces Fed test – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY sees Latin American (LatAm) assets benefiting again from improved terms of trade for energy and soft commodity exporters, with strong real-rate anchors supporting currencies and duration.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Bulls eye 0.8200 as rally extends
item.description: The USD/CHF extends its advance for the sixth straight trading session, up 0.11%, as the Greenback holds firm against a basket of six currencies, the US Dollar Index (DXY). At the time of writing, the pair trades at 0.8190, with buyers targeting 0.8200.

item.title: Gold rises toward $4,070 as falling US yields support Bullion
item.description: Gold price registers gains of 0.58% as Washington pauses attacks on Tehran, while US President Donald Trump opened the door for a resumption in negotiations. This, along with falling US Treasury yields, is a tailwind for Bullion prices with XAU/USD approaching $4,070.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Could Fed decision trigger a break from $55-$62 range?
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) reverses part of its earlier gains on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) rebounds after opening the week with a bearish gap following a temporary pause in attacks between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Germany: Recovery potential versus energy drag – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Dr. Jörg Krämer argues that high energy prices will continue to weigh on the German economy in the second half of 2026, limiting full-year growth to 0.6%.
